recipes.name: Hidden Treasures Ranch Pockets
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup warm water (110 degrees F to 115 degrees F)
1.5 cups bread flour, or as needed
1 (1 ounce) package ranch dressing mix (such as Hidden Valley Ranch®)
0.5 cup red bell pepper, finely chopped
1 teaspoon minced garlic, or to taste

steps.text: Sprinkle the yeast over warm water in a large bowl bowl. Let stand for 5 minutes until the yeast softens and begins to form a creamy foam. Beat in the sugar, egg, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and whole wheat flour with an electric mixer on low for 3 minutes. Stir in the bread flour, a 1/2 cup at a time, mixing well after each addition. When the dough has pulled together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes. Lightly oil a large bowl, then place the dough in the bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a light cloth and let rise in a warm place (80 to 95 degrees F (27 to 35 degrees C)) until doubled in volume, about 30 minutes.

While the dough is rising, heat a large skillet over medium heat and cook and stir until the pork is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Drain and discard any excess grease. Stir in the ranch dressing mix until meat is well-coated. Add the cabbage, zucchini, onion, red bell pepper, carrot, and garlic. Cook and stir until the vegetables are tender and most of the liquid has evaporated, about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.

Deflate the dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Use a knife to divide the dough into four equal pieces-don't tear it. Roll each portion out to an 8-inch square, then cut each large square into four smaller squares. Place about 3 tablespoonfuls of the pork filling into the center of each square. Bring the corners over the filling and pinch to seal. Secure with a toothpick, if needed. Spray a baking sheet with cooking spray. Place the pouches on the prepared baking sheet about 3-inches apart. Cover the pouches with a damp cloth and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 30 minutes.
Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 15 minutes. Remove from pan and discard toothpicks. Brush each pocket with melted butter. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Hidden Treasures Ranch Pockets
raw_recipe.description: This delicious and easy recipe is a great way to get your family to eat more veggies. The filling contains zucchini, carrots, cabbage, red pepper, onions, and garlic, yet still tastes so yummy that even the pickiest eaters gobble them up!

review.reviewBody: wow this was awesome...i was pressed for time and used phylo dough. this is great as left-overs, if you have any! ya give this a shot terrific way to get some veggies out of the garden and into those discerning rug rats! thx larkspur!

These were very tasty. I used my bread machine to make the dough which made it easier. I used ground beef instead of pork. And I mistakenly chopped my carrots finely instead of shredding them, I also used extra carrot. I made sure there was enough seasoning before filling the dough and I did add more ranch mix.

Used Grands biscuits, no zucchini, no red bell pepper and garlic powder....this changes due to not having the other ingredients and I didn't have time to go to the store. I used extra carrot and cabbage to compensate. My 5 children, ages 8-17, LOVED this recipe. The 10-year-old said we should have this every week. Was super easy with the biscuits, and because the grands are so good, I decided not to use butter, which was fine. I look forward to adding the zucchini and pepper next time. I think the pepper will be a yummy addition. Have printed out the recipe for my cookbook and a friend...it was that popular with my kiddos.

This was a simple and great recipe! The only reason I didn't give 5 stars was because I think the recipe could have just called for biscuit dough instead of going through all those steps. My hubby always says that there is no way I can get him to eat veggies. Well I did last night! It was fantastic! I was so surprised! Even my picky 2 yr old loved them! I created exactly minus the dough. I used Grands Biscuits. Turned out awesome! My hubby took ALL the leftovers to work!

I tried these the other day... what a hit they were, the kids loved them. They even were delicious cold. I didn't make the bread though, I instead used Won Ton wraps and they were delicious. Next time though I will brush them with the butter before putting them in the oven.

I too used refrigerated biscuit dough instead of using the recipe's. It was super simple this way to stuff them. I used an onion, 1/2 bellpepper, and a small bag of rainbow slaw mix for the cabbage/carrot (no zucchini on hand). We really liked the flavor that the ranch mix gave to the filling. These are the perfect size for a grab and go breakfast, and the possibilities for the fillings are endless!
In stead of doing all the work for the bread I used two croissant rolls.
I used a biscuit dough for the crust. Otherwise I followed the recipe. I did skip the ground pork and added more vegetables to the filling. This came out great and I will definitely make it again.
I made it into a pie with refrigerated dough to save time and used a homemade ranch mix (though it didn't taste ranch-y at all!). We thought it was just okay, and did make the recipe as-is.

Amazing! I used it more as a guideline, added flax seed to the bread (no whole wheat), and didn’t have the exact ratios of meat to veggies— but it turned out very nicely! I loved it. I made a cheese roll-up for my husband with a cheese stick, who doesn’t eat pork, which turned out well also, although some cheese leaked out.
My family loves this....definitely making again.
I only used the bread, but it was wonderful! I stuffed mine with lunch meats and cheese.
I have not made this yet, but I need something new to take to work. Think I'll use turkey and spinach tortillas.
I made these just as instructed, but really did care for them. The recipe is a good recipe, but the taste didnt suit me. Probably just my taste buds this time...

I made these exactly as written, and they were worth the effort! So good! This is one of those recipes that has you saying "why didn't I think of that?" Very original and very, very tasty. These are kid friendly and freeze well. I make them in batches for the freezer. Perfect for a quick and easy 'good for you' addition to lunch boxes.

These were very tasty, just difficult to work the dough. I had a tough day for getting dough to rise - and the squares barely closed for me. I had a little of the groudn pork mixture left over, just couldn't get it all to fit in the dough - however the flavor was so good and everyone enjoyed these - and I followed the recipe exactly (except for using half ww flour & half bread flour - 1c each)
They were ok to me, but the hubby loved them. I followed the recipe as is.

Yum! These are beyond delicious. I really wanted to make these tonight, but I didn't have time after work to make the dough so I did use refrigerated biscuits. That worked quite well, but I will definitely make the dough next time to get the full effect. Awesome flavors and textures. Thanks so much, larkspur! :)
